movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Men raise and move arms freely, sometimes miming knife fights; women keep arms below shoulder level or on hips with palms outward
movement_profile.difficulty: beginner to advanced depending on mastery of steps and symbolic gestures
movement_profile.footwork: Triplet-based steps with counterclockwise rotation; includes intricciata (interlaced foot crossing), doppi e ondeggiati (double and undulating steps), and spiral movements
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Circular formation called rota, dancers move counterclockwise within it
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Hips emphasized especially by women; torso remains relatively still
movement_profile.partnering: Couple dance (man-woman, man-man, woman-woman); partners may hold hands or dance shoulder to shoulder depending on local custom
movement_profile.posture: Upright with independent upper and lower body movement; trunk mostly static while legs move energetically

signature_moves.description: Interlaced foot crossing steps alternating feet outside the other
signature_moves.name: Intricciata

signature_moves.description: Bird-like miming step at the circle's edge to entice partner inward
signature_moves.name: Illi Adornu

signature_moves.description: Step to interrupt partner's spiral movement, often used by women to evade courtship
signature_moves.name: Tagghjapassu

signature_moves.description: Mimed knife fight gestures with fingers, symbolizing challenge or courtship
signature_moves.name: Schermijata

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Lively and energetic with triplet rhythm
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid dancing outside the rota; respect the social role of the mastru i ballu; do not appropriate mimed gestures without understanding their cultural meaning

music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Triplet-based rhythms supporting lively, spiraling dance movements
music_profile.sound_description: The music features a lively triplet rhythm in 12/8 or 6/8 time, driven by the zampogna or organetto, punctuated by tamburello beats, with occasional melodic lines from the Calabrian lira or pipita, creating a festive and energetic soundscape that supports dynamic, spiraling dance movements.

basic_steps: Form a circle (rota) with other dancers.
Wait for the mastru i ballu to select partners.
Begin with triplet-based steps, moving counterclockwise.
Men raise and move arms freely; women keep arms low or on hips.
Gradually move closer to partner, optionally holding hands or dancing shoulder to shoulder.
Perform intricciata (interlaced steps) by crossing feet alternately.
Use illi adornu step to mimic bird flight, enticing partner inward.
Women may use tagghjapassu to interrupt partner's spiral movement.
teaching.formation: Circular formation called rota with dancers moving counterclockwise
teaching.level_notes: Beginners start with basic triplet steps and simple rotation; intermediate dancers add intricate foot crossing and mimed gestures; advanced dancers master spiral movements and symbolic steps.
